sources.terms: CC-BY-4.0 (record metadata). Cite: P. Radoglou-Grammatikis et al., IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics 18(3), 2022, doi:10.1109/TII.2021.3093905.
sources.notes: IEC 60870-5-104 Intrusion Detection Dataset, University of Western Macedonia. Each 7z archive holds, per entity, the whole traffic and an *_iec104_only.pcap filtered to the IEC 104 frames (no SYN, no ACK-only segments). The ReadMe names five virtual RTUs (IEC TestServer on Windows 7), two real RTU devices, QTester104 v2.1 as HMI and three Kali Linux attackers (Metasploit iec104 module, OpenMUC j60870). The ReadMe identifies the real RTUs neither by address nor by make or model. In the recordings all seven controlled stations (192.168.1.13, .19, .21, .22, .24, .25, .26) have MAC addresses of the VirtualBox range 08:00:27 and behave identically; none can be shown to be a physical device.

sources.notes: Issue 17209 attached iec104S_test.7z (SHA256 ce1f3e6c0205f016632ce6a843526660bbb1981222811539d03a198873b8cad0) with two pcapng files, extracted unchanged, and two XML logs of a protocol analyzer, not committed.
